content:
I have a formalization of the 0-1 Principle for comparator sorting networks (Knuth, TAOCP Vol 3, Section 5.3.4). The result: a comparator network sorts all inputs over any linearly ordered type if and only if it sorts all Boolean inputs.

Declarations (~215 lines total):

structure Comparator (n : Nat)        -- pair (i, j) with i < j < n
abbrev Network (n : Nat)              -- List (Comparator n)
def Comparator.apply                  -- swap if out of order
def Network.apply                     -- fold comparators
def Network.sorts (α)                 -- sorts all α-inputs
def Network.sorts_bool                -- sorts all Bool-inputs

lemma apply_comp_monotone             -- monotone f commutes with apply
theorem zero_one_principle            -- sorts_bool → sorts α

The proof is the standard contrapositive via threshold functions: if the network fails on some input, collapsing through a monotone threshold produces a Boolean input that also fails. Key Mathlib lemma used: Monotone.map_min/Monotone.map_max.

Dependencies: Mathlib.Order.Fin.Basic, Mathlib.Order.MinMax, Mathlib.Order.Monotone.Basic. No sorry. Linter passes.

Proposed location: Cslib/Algorithms/SortingNetwork/Basic.lean (or wherever makes sense in the CSLib tree)

I checked for existing work and found no sorting network formalization in Mathlib or CSLib, no open/closed PRs, and no Zulip discussions on the topic. CSLib has MergeSort but no comparator networks. Is there any in-progress work I should know about? Any thoughts on the location or API design?

Code: https://gist.github.com/queelius/67b025e60f77554c374b93beff58b337

Computational analysis performed with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic); all proofs machine-checked by Lean.

thanks for the link. i see Geoffrey Irving already has a 0-1 principle formalization in his AKS repo, and Wrenna Robson has comparator network work in her controlbits project. my formalization covers the same ground as Geoffrey's ZeroOne.lean, just smaller and standalone. happy to defer to whatever they think makes sense for CSLib. they know this domain much better than i do.
